question: What is the primary goal of community mobilisation in healthcare?

options.A: Empowering local populations to take collective action
options.B: Imposing medical solutions directly from federal agencies
options.C: Collecting monetary taxes for local clinic repairs
options.D: Replacing traditional healers with trained nurses

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on building local capacity so community members can drive their own health initiatives. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is community mobilisation considered superior to top-down health delivery?

options.A: It guarantees immediate eradication of all infectious diseases
options.B: It ensures interventions respect local culture and real needs
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for professional health workers
options.D: It requires zero financial resources from the government

explanation: Involving the community directly ensures that health programs align with their actual lifestyles and priorities. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which core principle ensures that marginalized groups have a voice?
explanation: Equity guarantees fair access and representation for vulnerable or silenced groups within the population. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h2)

question: A community health project fails because locals stop maintaining it after foreign donors leave. Which core principle was ignored?
explanation: Sustainability ensures that interventions survive and function independently after external support ends. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h2)

question: Who are considered key gatekeepers during community entry?
explanation: Traditional and religious authorities hold immense influence and must grant entry and blessing for health projects to succeed. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the main danger of skipping the community entry phase?

options.A: Receiving too much funding from international partners
options.B: Generating suspicion and resistance from local residents
options.C: Spreading infectious diseases faster through the clinic
options.D: Forcing nurses to work longer daily hours

explanation: Failing to consult local leaders breeds distrust, making the community hostile or indifferent to incoming health workers. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h3)

question: What tool is commonly used to gather qualitative data during a needs assessment?
explanation: Focus group discussions allow nurses to capture community perceptions, beliefs, and shared health concerns qualitatively. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h4)

question: A nurse conducts a house-to-house survey to find out why children are malnourished in a rural village. What action cycle phase is this?
explanation: Gathering data to uncover the root causes of health problems falls directly under needs assessment and diagnosis. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why is priority setting necessary during the planning phase?

options.A: Resources are usually limited compared to existing problems
options.B: Government policy forbids tackling more than one disease
options.C: Communities prefer to solve only minor health issues
options.D: Nurses are not allowed to work on weekends

explanation: Because financial, material, and human resources are scarce, communities must focus on the most pressing health threats first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h5)

question: Who should be actively involved in setting priorities during this phase?

options.B: Both health workers and community representatives
options.D: Only the local government chairman and health minister

explanation: Collaborative planning ensures that the community takes ownership of the chosen interventions from the start. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse during the implementation phase?
explanation: Nurses guide and support community members rather than dominating the execution of the project. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h6)

question: What helps maintain high community morale and participation during action implementation?

options.A: Changing project goals every single week
options.B: Relying exclusively on foreign volunteers for labor
options.C: Keeping all financial budgets hidden from the villagers
options.D: Transparent use of resources and clear communication

explanation: Transparency builds trust and encourages continuous community involvement in the planned activities. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by foreigners, evaluation by locals
options.B: Monitoring happens before planning, evaluation happens during entry
options.C: Monitoring is continuous, while evaluation assesses final outcomes
options.D: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is entirely free

explanation: Monitoring occurs throughout the project life, whereas evaluation looks back at the overall results and impact. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h7)

question: How do local maintenance committees contribute to project sustainability?

options.A: By writing academic research papers for universities
options.B: By managing ongoing activities after external workers leave
options.C: By stopping all future community health meetings
options.D: By collecting taxes to send to the federal government

explanation: Local committees ensure continuity by maintaining infrastructure and programs independently. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h7)

question: Which role does a nurse fulfill when translating complex health data for villagers?
explanation: As educators, nurses break down health concepts so community members can grasp and apply them. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: Why must nurses avoid creating dependency during the action cycle?

options.A: So nurses can retire from community service early
options.B: So the community can eventually manage health issues independently
options.C: So foreign NGOs will take over all clinic operations
options.D: So the government can cut the health sector budget

explanation: Promoting self-reliance ensures long-term sustainability and prevents the community from becoming helpless without external nurses. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)
